solver.kind: blind AI solver (separate agent, answer-free packet, rubric v2)

flags: minor: key paraphrases the thesis of paragraph 2 closely; B (fairness 'more than any other feature') is an extreme-wording distractor that test-wise students reject quickly
R015-01.notes: 'Half true': time matters, but so does how the wait feels (Maister's factors: uncertainty, fairness, etc.). A contradicts 'their work was valuable'; B overstated; D not stated.

flags: minor: key echoes paragraph 4 wording ('more bearable without making it any shorter') and paragraph 3 ('total time ... stayed about the same')
R015-02.notes: Critics object to managing perception without shortening the wait; airport kept total time the same. B contradicts 'stayed about the same'; C opposite; D unsupported.

R015-03.notes: Posted estimates remove uncertainty ('uncertain waits feel longer than waits of known length'). One-step mapping.

flags: minor: A ('empties quickly') may lure students who latch onto 'how the wait ended', but it still stalls 10 minutes, so it is a fair trap rather than a second defensible answer
R015-04.notes: Paragraph 6: steady movement and a good ending matter more than total length; D is the only line that advances steadily to the end. B ends with a stall; A and C stall-and-lurch.

R015-05.notes: 'stalls and then lurches forward' contrasted with advancing 'a little at a time' -> sudden, uneven movement. B is the literal-tilt dictionary trap; D is the opposite.

flags: minor: key is the longest and most qualified choice (length cue)
minor: 'influential' is inferred from 'most cited applications' rather than stated directly; D (neutral reporting) is the main competitor for students who see the passage as expository
R015-06.notes: Author frames the researchers' assumption as 'only half true', calls the memory finding 'most intriguing', and presents both critics and defenders -> favorable view plus acknowledged debate. B and C contradict the passage; D ignores the evaluative framing.

R015-07.notes: 'Waiting is partly a story we tell ourselves afterward' -> designers shape the remembered experience, not only the clock time. A and C take 'authors' literally; D contradicts the point that the clock matters little.

flags: minor: key nearly copies the passage wording ('someone who arrived later being served first'); B, C, D are direct reversals of Maister's points, so the item is a pure lookup
R015-08.notes: Paragraph 2: an unfair wait, with a later arrival served first, feels longer. Other choices describe conditions that make waits feel shorter.
